title: CFPGrasp: Coarse-to-Fine Prediction Network for 6-DoF Robotic Grasping With Improved Grasp Representation
abstract: Grasping objects plays a crucial role in robotic manipulation within industrial applications, with the primary goal being the prediction of the robot grasp pose for each target object. However, accurately predicting the grasp pose is challenging due to diverse object shapes, appearances, and sizes. Moreover, the inherent complexity of grasp parameters, together with the existence of multiple valid grasps per object, imposes substantial demands on reasoning. To address these challenges, we first introduce a physics-informed contact–rotation grasp representation that simplifies the pose space, and then adopt a coarse-to-fine prediction strategy that proposes contact candidates globally and refines their rotation and quality locally. Accordingly, we propose a coarse-to-fine prediction network for 6-DoF grasping prediction in this paper, which first detects the valid contact points of grasp pose in the global scene, then predicts its corresponding rotation angle and grasp quality in the local region. The evaluation results on simulation and real-world grasp datasets demonstrate the advantages and effectiveness of the proposed approach. We also conduct a practical grasping experiment to show its generalization performance in real-world robotic grasping.

# 一、动机

> 6-DoF 抓取姿态预测受物体形状、外观、尺寸多样，以及抓取参数复杂和同一物体存在多个有效抓取的影响，推理负担大，难以准确预测。


# 二、方法

> 提出物理启发的接触-旋转抓取表示来简化姿态空间，并采用由粗到细预测网络：先在全局场景中检测有效接触点，再在局部区域预测旋转角与抓取质量。
